text.p: Compagnie Financiere Richemont AG, the Swiss-based concern active mainly in tobacco and luxury goods sectors, said profit attributable to unitholders fell 4.2 percent to 302.9 million stg in the year ended March 31, 1997.
It said net sales revenue was up 10.4 percent at 4.756 billion stg from 4.307 billion in the previous year.
It said that its dividend per unit was increased to 9.40 stg for the year completed from 8.00 stg for the previous year.
Richemont said that the reported profit was adjusted to exclude exceptional items and goodwill amortisation.
"These results reflected in particular the substantial increase in losses incurred by the Group's media interests," Richemont said in a statement to present its results.
"In addition, the results were adversely impacted by the strength of sterling in the year under review, which reduced attributable profit by some 29 million stg," it said.
"On an underlying basis, therefore, the Group's tobacco and luxury goods businesses achieved satisfactory growth," it said.
Richemont's tobacco interests are held through Rothmans International, whose brands include Rothmans, Dunhill, Peter Stuyvesant and Craven "A".
Its luxury goods brands besides Dunhill include Cartier, Montblanc, Piaget, Baume & Mercier and Vacheron Constantin.

A merger of its electronic media interests in NetHold, held jointly by Richemont and MIH Holdings with Canal Plus , the French pay television operator, resulted in Richemont holding 15 percent in the enlarged media concern.

Richemont said the acquisition of an interest in Canal Plus as a result of the merger with NetHold was the principal factor behind an increase of 202.1 million stg in investments in associated undertakings, which rose to 605 million stg in the 1996/97 year.
It said that continued subscriber growth in the media sector resulted in substantially higher revenues.

But, it added, "the investment necessary to support the further development of NetHold's business meant that Richemont's share of operating losses from media activities increased by 34.7 million stg to 81.0 million stg." -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
